security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU TCG advertises Ziccid in ISA string but does not flush/invalidate stale TranslationBlocks for cacheable+coherent memory regions when another hart modifies instruction memory without an explicit FENCE.I. Ziccid requires that stores eventually become visible to all harts' instruction fetches; in QEMU TCG this translates to eventually invalidating cached TBs for modified guest code pages. If QEMU relies solely on FENCE.I-triggered TB flushes and lacks a mechanism (e.g., periodic or write-triggered TB invalidation on cross-hart stores to executable pages) to ensure eventual visibility, a guest JIT compiler thread storing new code will have its stores indefinitely invisible to other harts' instruction fetches, causing those harts to execute stale (pre-modification) translated host code.
security_spec.summary: QEMU TCG TranslationBlock cache may serve stale host code indefinitely after cross-hart guest code modification when Ziccid is advertised, violating Ziccid's store-to-instruction-fetch eventual-visibility guarantee

findings.finding: Ziccid is NOT present in isa_edata_arr. QEMU correctly does not advertise 'ziccid' in the ISA string since Ziccid is not a ratified RISC-V extension — it only appears in RVA23/RVB23 profile notes as a possible future option. Adding ziccid to the ISA string without implementing Ziccid-specific coherence semantics would be a bug, but no such addition is present.

spec_citations.excerpt: NOTE: ext:zifencei[] is mandated as it is the only standard way to support instruction-cache coherence in RVA23 application processors. A new instruction-cache coherence mechanism, ext:ziccid[], might be added as an option in the future.

findings.finding: No ext_ziccid field exists in RISCVCPUConfig. There is no config knob to enable Ziccid, consistent with the extension not being ratified. The closest cache-related fields are ext_ziccrse and the Zicbom/Zicboz/Zicbop extensions (ext_zicbom, ext_zicboz, ext_zicbop).

The generic TCG notdirty_write mechanism provides eventual cross-hart instruction-fetch visibility: on the first write to any RAM page marked clean for code tracking, tb_invalidate_phys_range_fast() is called, which globally invalidates all TBs on all vCPUs for the affected physical range via do_tb_phys_invalidate() — removing from the global htable, all CPU jmp caches, and all jmp lists. This functionally achieves what Ziccid would require (eventual instruction-fetch coherence without explicit FENCE.I), though it is a general QEMU mechanism rather than RISC-V-specific Ziccid implementation.

spec_citations.excerpt: FENCE.I does not ensure that other RISC-V harts' instruction fetches will observe the local hart's stores in a multiprocessor system. To make a store to instruction memory visible to all RISC-V harts, the writing hart also has to execute a data FENCE before requesting that all remote RISC-V harts execute a FENCE.I.

findings.finding: do_tb_phys_invalidate() performs complete global TB invalidation: removes from tb_ctx.htable (global hash), removes from all CPU jmp caches via CPU_FOREACH in tb_jmp_cache_inval_tb(), removes from page list, and unlinks from all jump chains. This ensures that after a write to a code page, no hart can execute the stale TB through any fast-path lookup. The mechanism provides the eventual-visibility guarantee Ziccid would require.

FENCE.I is correctly implemented as a TB-ending no-op in QEMU TCG. The comment explains: 'FENCE_I is a no-op in QEMU, however we need to end the translation block.' This is correct because QEMU has no emulated I-cache — TB invalidation is handled by the generic notdirty_write mechanism on actual writes to code pages. FENCE.I does NOT flush TBs globally (it only ends the current TB), but this is correct per spec: FENCE.I only synchronizes a single hart's instruction fetches with its own prior stores. Cross-hart coherence requires additional FENCE + IPI + remote FENCE.I, which is a guest software responsibility.

spec_citations.excerpt: RISC-V does not guarantee that stores to instruction memory will be made visible to instruction fetches on a RISC-V hart until that hart executes a FENCE.I instruction. FENCE.I does not ensure that other RISC-V harts' instruction fetches will observe the local hart's stores in a multiprocessor system.

findings.finding: ISA string construction correctly excludes ziccid since no entry exists in isa_edata_arr. The ISA string will contain zifencei (if enabled) but not ziccid. This is correct behavior for an unratified extension.
